1. (Currently Amended) An ophthalmic illumination system, comprising a light source operable to generate a source light beam; a beam splitter operable to split the source light beam into a first light beam and a second light beam; a first attenuator located in a path of the first light beam, the first attenuator operable to change an intensity of the first light beam; a second attenuator located in a path of the second light beam, the second attenuator operable to change an intensity of the second light beam; a first optical fiber port configured for connection to a first optical fiber, the first optical fiber delivering at least a portion of the first light beam to a patient's eye; a second optical fiber port configured for connection to a second optical fiber, the second optical fiber delivering at least a portion of the second light beam to the patient's eye; and a control unit communicatively coupled to the first attenuator and the second attenuator, the control unit operable to: adjust the first attenuator in order to control the intensity of the portion of the first light beam delivered to the patient's eye via the first optical fiber independently of the second attenuator; and adjust the second attenuator to control the intensity of the portion of the second light beam delivered to the patient's eye via the second optical fiber independently of the first attenuator.

9. (Currently Amended) The ophthalmic illumination system of claim 1, further comprising: a first power monitor operable to receive at least a portion of the first light beam exiting the first attenuator, the first power monitor operable to generate a first feedback signal corresponding to the intensity of the first light beam; and a second power monitor operable to receive at least a portion of the second light beam exiting the second attenuator, the second power monitor operable to generate a second feedback signal corresponding to the intensity of the second light beam, wherein the first power monitor and second power monitor are physically separate and distinct components.

10. (Currently Amended) The ophthalmic illumination system of claim 9, wherein the controller is further operable to: adjust the first attenuator based at least in part on the first feedback signal corresponding to the intensity of the first light beam generated by the first power monitor; and adjust the second attenuator based at least in part on the second feedback signal corresponding to the intensity of the second light beam generated by the second power monitor.

11. (Currently Amended) The ophthalmic illumination system of claim 1, wherein the first optical fiber and the second optical fiber each comprise a nano fiber having a core diameter of 25 μm or less, wherein the nano fibers are configured to deliver light to distinct anatomical regions of the patient's eye.

12. (Currently Amended) The ophthalmic illumination system of claim 1, wherein: the first optical fiber is integrated with a first surgical instrument connected to the first port, the first surgical instrument being a specialized illumination delivery instrument; the second optical fiber is integrated with a second surgical instrument connected to the second port, the second surgical instrument being a specialized illumination delivery instrument distinct from the first surgical instrument; the first surgical instrument and the second surgical instrument each comprise one of a sclerotomy cannula, a vitreous cutter, an illumination probe, forceps, scissors, a spatula, and a pic; and the first surgical instrument and the second surgical instrument are configured to deliver light to different anatomical locations within the patient's eye simultaneously.
